query: Explain the attached job queue implementation. I added this queue and want to understand its central rule, not just trust it. I am comfortable with the app but new to queues.
expected_behavior: Treats this as a concept explainer for the operator, not documentation for the repo
Uses the supplied implementation and names `runOne`, `store.ack`, and `store.release` accurately
Explains the load-bearing rule: a job is acknowledged only after its handler succeeds, while a failed handler releases it with an incremented attempt count
Writes for a reader comfortable with the app but new to queues
Offers an optional predict-then-reveal or checked exercise without forcing it or leaking the answer
Ends with a prediction the reader could make about what happens when the handler throws
